done.why: I was on my way back from a dead-end beach to try the stairs in the Loud Room when the world told me I'd used all 30 turns. I wasn't bored yet, but I was close: the beach had nothing but a river I couldn't enter, and I'd just spent six turns walking out and back for it.

about: A white house in a field with a hidden way down into caves under it. You grab a lamp and a sword, drop through a trap door that someone bars behind you, kill a troll, and then wander a cave system where a lot of the passages have collapsed. There's a huge rushing-water sound somewhere and a cold grey river at the bottom of white cliffs; I think the real game is about that water, a dam or something, but I never got to it.

moments.note: The leaflet just says 'welcome to Zork, no computer should be without one.' Fine, but it told me nothing about what to do.
The trap door crashes shut and 'you hear someone barring it.' Who? That got my attention, and then the sword started glowing.
Swung at the troll, missed, got knocked to my knees. Four turns of typing the same line was a lot for an impatient person.
'It's curtains for the troll as your sword removes his head,' then the body vanishes in black fog. Good payoff.
Round Room says several passages are blocked by cave-ins. So this place is broken on purpose; made me wonder what else is different.
Tried to take the platinum bar and the room just echoed 'Bar bar ...' back at me. I get that it's a joke about the noise, but I wanted the bar.
The river description: in a hurry, as if it had heard something about the end of it and wanted to see for itself. Best line in the whole thing.
'Swimming isn't usually allowed in the dungeon.' So the beach is a dead end with a pretty river I can look at and nothing else. Then the cap hit while I was walking back.

wished: Get into or onto the river somehow; the beach has nothing else and the river is described so well it feels like it wants you to.
Pick up the platinum bar, or be told how to shut the noise up so I could.
Know who barred the trap door behind me; it was the most interesting thing that happened and nothing followed it up.
Some sense of which Round Room passages were caved in without having to try each one.
A few more turns; 30 is barely enough to get through the house and past the troll.

lines.line: The trap door crashes shut, and you hear someone barring it.
lines.why: First moment I felt like something was happening to me rather than me just walking around. Someone is up there.

lines.line: It's curtains for the troll as your sword removes his head.
lines.why: After three failed swings this was the relief and the laugh at once.

lines.line: Several of them have unfortunately been blocked by cave-ins.
lines.why: Told me this version of the caves is damaged, which made the rushing-water sound in the next room feel like a threat instead of set dressing.

lines.line: The Frigid River is wide and grey and very cold, and in a hurry, going downstream as if it had heard something about the end of it and wanted to see for itself.
lines.why: The one line with real personality. It made me want to follow the river, which I then couldn't do.

lines.line: Swimming isn't usually allowed in the dungeon.
lines.why: The flat no that ended my only lead.

fun.why: The troll fight and the slammed trap door were fun; the beach dead end and the echo-room refusing me the bar were not. It was a decent few minutes, not a great one.

engagement.why: I kept going because the glowing sword and the barred door promised something. But six turns spent walking to a beach and back with nothing to do there was draining the goodwill, and the cap hit before I found the stairs.

difficulty.why: Nothing I did was hard to figure out; the house and troll were straightforward. The troll fight took four identical swings, which is tedium not difficulty, and the real puzzles (river, bar, noise) I never got a handle on.

interestingness.why: The cave-ins and the unseen person barring the door suggest a changed, damaged version of a place, and the rushing sound and river hint at a dam story. I only saw the edges of it.

prose.why: Mostly plain and functional, but the river and cliffs descriptions and the troll's death line have real snap. 'Bar bar ...' is a clever joke even though it annoyed me.
